title: Bubbles in boiling water: which of the four, if any?
question: Which of these reads as water boiling rather than as speckle on the water -- and is any of them better than leaving it off?
context_md:
The pending `BubbleMode` default. Four modes behind `,` in the app, `Off` today. `filmstrip scene=boil` -- a walled chamber of water under a burning oil slick -- at frames 150, 270, 390, with gas drawn translucent so you can see the pool through the steam.

One thing worth knowing before you look, because it decides *where* you can judge this: **`Surface` draws literally nothing on a pan heated from below.** Diffed pixel-for-pixel against `Off` on `scene=simmer` and on `scene=lavadrop`: **0 pixels differ** in both. It gates on the cell being within a couple of rows of the top of its own body, and on anything heated from underneath the hot water is at the bottom -- the same trap `BUBBLE_MIN_TEMPERATURE` was lowered to 40C to escape. It only has anything to draw here, where the heat is a slick floating on top. So if you like it, it is a mode that shows up in roughly one situation.

Changed pixels against `Off` on this scene: Rising 5,975, Columns 4,450, Surface 5,125 -- so all three are firing, and none of them is being judged blank.

items.label: B
